assertion.normalizations: Integer multipliers clear the modular coefficient ambiguities before inversion.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An O(X) translation is retained in weighted coefficient bookkeeping; unbounded affine step is excluded.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the substitution bounds and degree before varying X.

assertion.parameter_range: All integer exponents, all real coordinate parameters, all permitted finite alphabet sizes, including zero survivors.

assertion.statement: For the actual rational homomorphism rho:U->G, one positive integer D can be chosen so that rho(exp(D L0)) is contained in Gamma, while remaining divisible by the integer already required for BCH closure.
assertion.objects: The fixed simply connected nilpotent U and G, rational homomorphism rho, homogeneous rational basis of Lie(U), its integer span L0, and a rational Malcev basis of G adapted to Gamma.
assertion.hypotheses: The preceding construction supplies rational rho and the stated rational bases. BCH closure and cocompactness of exp(D L0) are supplied separately by the displayed local proof.
assertion.quantifiers: Every x in L0 for one D chosen from the finitely many coordinate polynomials of this fixed construction.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed finite-dimensional nilpotent groups and fixed rational bases; no varying-family denominator estimate.
assertion.uniformity: The same D works for all integer coordinate vectors x in L0 within this fixed construction.
assertion.constants: D is a common positive multiple of coordinate-polynomial denominators and the prior BCH denominator requirement.
assertion.normalizations: Second-kind Malcev coordinates identify Gamma exactly with integer vectors; rho(exp x)=exp(d rho(x)).
assertion.exceptional_cases: Every coordinate polynomial has zero constant term because rho maps identity to identity. Thus scaling variables by D clears denominators in every nonzero-degree monomial; no assertion that an arbitrary polynomial with nonintegral constant can be so scaled.
assertion.limit_order: Fix rho and bases; write the finite rational coordinate polynomials; choose one common multiple D; then evaluate on every integer vector. Increasing D preserves denominator divisibility.

assertion.hypotheses: Original structural data are standard; F is a bounded Lipschitz limit function with a standard vertical character; coefficients may be limit coefficients.

assertion.parameter_range: All integer inputs; arbitrary standard s,m>=1.
assertion.uniformity: The same quotient and metric constants for all members; no choice of a new nilmanifold from each large coefficient.
assertion.constants: Exact representation, no correlation loss, approximation error or norm rescaling.
assertion.normalizations: Symbol relation is lower-degree tensor quotient, with the two required conjugations.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Limit representatives may be restricted to an ultrafilter-large set on which the exact defining identities hold.
assertion.limit_order: Fix structural data, normalize each polynomial within one compact set, use the uniform geometric construction, and then take the limit.

assertion.statement: Positive binomial coefficient estimates transfer through a bounded-step integer affine map with an O(N) offset after one standard denominator multiplier.
assertion.objects: Real horizontal polynomial f, transformed polynomial f(A+bm), positive binomial coefficients and their circle norms.
assertion.hypotheses: One variable, fixed degree, nonzero bounded integer b, |A|=O(N), transformed positive degree-j coefficient O(N^-j) modulo integers.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such internal polynomial and progression, with one standard multiplier for all positive coefficients.
assertion.parameter_range: k=1 in the general MF-AFFINE lemma; dense progression length comparable to N in DF002.
assertion.uniformity: Denominator depends on fixed degree and bounded step, not the offset or integer parts of coefficients.
assertion.constants: Inverse coefficient from degree j to positive degree i is O(N^(j-i)); residual O(N^-j) therefore gives O(N^-i).
assertion.normalizations: Clear the common rational denominator before reducing modulo integers; no bound is required for degree zero.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Negative nonzero b is allowed; multiplying the nonzero horizontal character by a positive standard integer preserves nonzeroness.
assertion.limit_order: Fix geometry, degree and progression step bound; choose the standard denominator multiplier; transfer all positive estimates simultaneously.

assertion.statement: The same-field maximal-order CM factor Eprime has original stable height equal to the average of -log(2pi)-2log|eta(tau)|-(1/2)log Im(tau) after a good-reduction extension.
assertion.objects: The actual Eprime/L from the maximal-order quotient, with fundamental discriminant Delta_F; its individual complex embeddings.
assertion.hypotheses: Eprime is a CM elliptic curve, hence potentially everywhere good; the analytic discriminant formula applies to each embedding and the finite discriminant term vanishes on the good-reduction extension.
assertion.quantifiers: Every embedding of a field where Eprime has everywhere good reduction; average with division by its absolute degree.
assertion.parameter_range: CM elliptic curves over number fields, with reduced imaginary-quadratic periods.
assertion.uniformity: Stable height is unchanged by the auxiliary good-reduction extension, whose degree never enters the later isogeny bound.
assertion.constants: Analytic discriminant (2pi)^12 eta(tau)^24; sqrt(3)/2<=Im(tau)<=sqrt(|Delta_F|)/2.
assertion.normalizations: Original stable Faltings metric; individual-embedding equation6.2, not the class-average Proposition6.1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No Weierstrass-coefficient condition over Q(j) is imported from Proposition6.1; the auxiliary good-reduction field is not the isogeny field L.
assertion.limit_order: Construct Eprime over L, pass to a good-reduction extension only to evaluate stable height, apply the individual formula, and return to the same L for the isogeny estimate.

assertion.statement: The D210 maximal Shimura curve quotient X/W is the rational contact line with precisely five index-two branch points, labelled210,105,70,42,30 at infinity,0,1,2401,−343/32 respectively.
assertion.objects: The genus-five maximal-level curve X, its rational Atkin-Lehner group W=(Z/2)^4, and the four published genus-one quotient models.
assertion.hypotheses: The published GR2006 quotient equations, genus and Atkin-Lehner group law are supplied; use characteristic-zero cyclic stabilizers and Riemann-Hurwitz. The exact rational quartic-invariant and cross-ratio computation is retained separately.
assertion.quantifiers: All branch orbits of the full W quotient, not merely the four initially supplied involutions.
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed quaternion discriminant210 and the four involutions30,42,70,105.
assertion.uniformity: The labelled quotient identification is fixed before choosing the rational contact parameter.
assertion.constants: Genus5, group order16, fixed-point total40, five branch orbits each of size8 and inertia2; coordinates2401 and−343/32.
assertion.normalizations: Choose labels210,105,70 at infinity,0,1. Quartic invariants I=12ae−3bd+c², J=72ace+9bcd−27ad²−27b²e−2c³, j=6912I³/(4I³−J²).
assertion.exceptional_cases: This characteristic-zero branch identification does not itself prove the integral tame model or the level-three fine cover. The exact coordinate computation remains a separate finite input.
assertion.limit_order: Use the four genus-one quotients to count fixed points; deduce quotient genus and fifth inertia label; identify rational branch sections; apply exact quartic/cross-ratio calculations to fix the remaining coordinates.

assertion.statement: For the unbranched rational contact-line point s, the entire principal-level-three D210 fiber has a normal splitting field L/Q with [L:Q] dividing576. Its abelian surfaces and all geometric homomorphisms between them are defined over L, and rad(D_L N_bad) divides B_* M_5(s).
assertion.objects: The entire canonical principal-level-three scheme Y of the maximal quaternion order of discriminant210, its fiber over s, the constant normalizer group Gamma, the actual normal splitting field L, and the universal fiber surfaces with full three-torsion markings.
assertion.hypotheses: The full fine-cover construction, canonical rational normalizer action and five-section contact-line identification are supplied. The selected rational s avoids the branch/contact set. The smooth tame quotient models away from210 and their local equations are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such rational s and every pair of fiber surfaces over the same full fiber splitting field.
assertion.parameter_range: Quaternion discriminant210; level3 is ramified in the quaternion algebra; all arithmetic components of the cover are included.
assertion.uniformity: The degree bound576 and the ramification support bound hold for every permitted s without choosing or adjoining a further field for geometric homomorphisms.
assertion.constants: Degree over stack72, generic coarse degree36; |W|=16; |Gamma|=576; B_*=product of primes at most76176.
assertion.normalizations: Use the whole canonical model and its regular action, not one complex component. The Galois image lies in the regular centralizer. Hom is the integral geometric Hom lattice; congruence modulo3 applies after all fiber3-torsion markings are defined.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No application of a prime-to-discriminant level theorem at3. The height calculation at bad primes uses the maximal stack separately. This does not construct Lprime, normalize the modular representation, or prove a numerical Faltings-height bound.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the whole fine cover and canonical action; choose s; split its finite fiber; descend all Hom using the same L; apply tame local contact equations to the ramification and reduction support.

assertion.statement: For the actual non-CM conjugate D210 fiber surfaces A and A_sigma, the normalizer action gives a geometric isogeny; the full geometric endomorphism algebra is B. For prescribed embeddings of the same quadratic field F, an isogeny intertwining those embeddings exists over the same fiber field L.
assertion.objects: Actual conjugate fiber surfaces of the entire principal-level-three curve, their rank-one left-B rational Hodge objects, geometric Hom lattices, and the prescribed two embeddings of F.
assertion.hypotheses: The full PEL/normalizer comparison and same-L Hom descent are supplied. A is non-CM. The rational Hodge equivalence and Skolem-Noether for the simple subalgebra embeddings are retained at their actual scopes.
assertion.quantifiers: Each conjugate surface in the same normalizer orbit and each pair of the prescribed embeddings of F.
assertion.parameter_range: Dimension-two quaternionic surfaces with B the rational division algebra of discriminant210.
assertion.uniformity: One and the same L defines all resulting geometric homomorphisms; no new field-degree cost.
assertion.constants: No quantitative isogeny-degree estimate or coherent cocycle bound is asserted.
assertion.normalizations: A finite-adelic move changes only a commensurable integral lattice in the same rational Hodge object. Use torsion density and invariant graph descent to obtain the geometric map, then clear rational Hom denominators after inner conjugation.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The F-linear isogenies need not be chosen coherently. This does not construct the later B-linear scalar-normalizer maps, sign splitting, compatible family, or bounded descent to a rational GL2-type variety.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the complex isogeny by finite torsion quotient; descend its graph geometrically; identify End^0=B in the non-CM case; apply Skolem-Noether, clear denominators and use the already fixed Hom field L.

assertion.statement: The same full-marking scheme Y_Q is the entire canonical principal-level U(3) Shimura curve, with maximal-level forgetful map and canonical normalizer action; its generic coarse degree is36.
assertion.objects: All arithmetic components of Y_Q, the quaternionic type-C1 rational Hodge datum and full finite-adelic U(3) marking orbit.
assertion.hypotheses: The full representable marking scheme and its universal surface are supplied; the exact Milne Hodge-orbit, algebraic family, canonical-model and uniqueness criteria and the integral principal-polarization assertion are retained.
assertion.quantifiers: Every component and every marked geometric object of the full functor, compatibly with all automorphisms of C/Q.
assertion.parameter_range: Discriminant210, principal full level3, reflex fieldQ; both real half-planes and all unit marking multipliers.
assertion.uniformity: The comparison is for the entire Q-model and commutes with level forgetting and normalizer action.
assertion.constants: Stack degree72 and generic coarse degree36 after quotienting central signs; no extra field or level introduced.
assertion.normalizations: Compatible alternating forms have a full Q-times similitude class. The actual positive polarization representative is chosen only at the integral-object stage. Galois comparison uses algebraic torsion data, not rational Betti cohomology.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No uncorrected general implication from Milne8.14/8.17; verify the type-C1 full Hodge orbit directly. No positive-multiplier subgroup or fixed mod3 pairing value is substituted. CM and reciprocity ancestry of the canonical criterion remains a source input.
assertion.limit_order: Verify compatible forms and full Hodge orbit; match integral Tate lattices through finite torsion quotients; construct algebraic families and markings on every component; apply the exact canonical Q-model criterion and uniqueness.

assertion.statement: The covariant rational Hodge equivalence identifies the full rational Hodge endomorphisms of the actual complex surface with its full complex algebraic endomorphisms; with the separately supplied centralizer calculation and geometric descent this yields End^0_Qbar(A)=B in the non-CM branch.
assertion.objects: The actual D210 surface A, its covariant H1(A(C),Q), rank-one left B action and right complex structure J; likewise its conjugate A_sigma.
assertion.hypotheses: A is a complex abelian surface with polarizable weight-minus-one homology. The rank-one B centralizer calculation, the non-CM choice K0=Q, and descent of complex homomorphisms to Qbar are separate retained inputs.
assertion.quantifiers: For each actual surface and every rational Hodge endomorphism; all endomorphisms, not just those preserving the chosen polarization.
assertion.parameter_range: Complex abelian varieties up to isogeny, Hodge types (-1,0),(0,-1); the current application is the non-CM D210 surface.
assertion.uniformity: No varying-field or effective uniform bound is supplied.
assertion.constants: No degree, conductor or height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Covariant H1 and Hom tensored with Q; a polarization is an existence condition on objects, not a restriction to polarization-preserving morphisms.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The imaginary-quadratic centralizer is the CM branch and is excluded here. Hodge equivalence alone supplies neither Qbar descent nor End=B without the centralizer calculation.
assertion.limit_order: First compute the rational Hodge centralizer, select the non-CM branch, then use algebraicity and the separate geometric descent.

assertion.statement: For the actual final primitive D210 form and R, its level satisfies N≤210^300 R^2 and rad(N) divides R.
assertion.objects: The same r_ell and primitive f, E=L(A[11]), the kernel field Q(chi), and the quadratic-kernel extension Fprime of their compositum.
assertion.hypotheses: E/Q is Galois with degree<2^66 and A has good reduction over E at2,3,5,7; chi is tame at odd primes with2-part conductor at most4; b restricts quadratically and normally as stated; actual local conductor equals v_p(N). Ramification/different and Artin conductor conventions are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational p using an auxiliary ell different from p for the actual family.
assertion.parameter_range: Small primes2,3,5,7 and all p>7; no bound on the full tame ramification index is assumed.
assertion.uniformity: Bounds use only R and the fixed degree/character constraints, not a bounded coefficient-field degree.
assertion.constants: v_p(e_Fprime)≤65 for3,5,7 and≤67 for2; largest positive upper break≤136; Swan≤272; total conductor≤274<300 at small primes,≤2 above7 and0 outside support.
assertion.normalizations: Q(chi) is its kernel field, not value field. Full conductor includes tame and Swan terms without semisimplifying inertia.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Unbounded tame ramification is allowed. Separate torsion good reduction and prime-to11 isogeny argument establish the required Galois E; this connection does not assume them proved merely from the degree estimate.
assertion.limit_order: Construct E and the normal splitting extensions; bound wild p-part indices and upper breaks; bound the actual conductor; transfer to level via the all-prime comparison.

assertion.statement: For the two specified embeddings i,j of the same quadratic field F into B, inner conjugation gives b in B^times with j(x)=b^-1 i(x)b for every x in F; applied to j=f^-1 i_sigma f, the quasi-isogeny f b^-1 intertwines the specified F actions.
assertion.objects: The quaternion algebra B/Q=End^0_Qbar(A), abstract quadratic F and specified embeddings i:F→B and j=f^-1 i_sigma f:F→B.
assertion.hypotheses: B is the full non-CM endomorphism algebra; f:A→A_sigma is an independently supplied geometric quasi-isogeny, and i,i_sigma are the actual specified actions. The induced map i(x)→j(x) is a Q-algebra isomorphism of quadratic subfields.
assertion.quantifiers: For these embeddings there exists an invertible b implementing their specified field identification on every x.
assertion.parameter_range: Quadratic subfields of the characteristic-zero quaternion algebra B/Q.
assertion.uniformity: Existence for each pair only; no uniform degree or coherent choices in sigma.
assertion.constants: No quantitative bound is supplied.
assertion.normalizations: j=b^-1 i b and g=f b^-1; quasi-homomorphisms are rationalized Hom. Positive integer denominator clearing is a separate elementary step.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An unspecified conjugacy of unlabelled subfields is insufficient. b need not be integral. The official erratum corrects unit-group notation after separable extension; no inseparable case or deleted optional splitting-field parenthesis is used.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain f and full End=B first; conjugate the specified embeddings, then clear denominators. Same-L descent, compatibility, cocycles, Q-descent and quantitative bounds are separate.

assertion.statement: The actual D210 quaternionic surface has potentially good reduction everywhere, and E=L(A[11]) is Galois over Q with [E:Q]<2^66; A has good reduction over E at every residue characteristic different from11.
assertion.objects: The actual A/L with rational quaternion division action and all geometric Hom over the normal fiber field L, its full11-torsion field E and the semistable special-fiber torus.
assertion.hypotheses: The D210 normalizer and same-L Hom construction are supplied. The published semistable reduction and full-torsion criteria, Neron extension property and torus structure are retained. The normalizer maps can be scaled prime to11 using the split maximal order at11.
assertion.quantifiers: Every place of A, and every conjugate of the full torsion field E; the good-reduction conclusion over E is for residue characteristics other than11.
assertion.parameter_range: Dimension two, division quaternion algebra B of discriminant210, degree[L:Q]≤576 and auxiliary prime11.
assertion.uniformity: The same Galois field E suffices simultaneously at2,3,5,7; no unbounded new extension is used for the later degree estimate.
assertion.normalizations: A positive torus rank t≤2 would give an injective unital B→M_t(Q), impossible for t=1 by dimension and for t=2 by division versus split algebra. Prime-to11 isogenies identify conjugate11-torsion kernels over L.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The full-torsion reduction criterion is not applied at residue characteristic11. Potential good reduction alone does not imply the explicit field E is Galois; that uses normalizer maps prime to11.
assertion.limit_order: Pass temporarily to semistable reduction and exclude torus rank; construct prime-to11 conjugate isogenies over L; prove E is Galois and bound its degree; apply the full11-torsion criterion and torus argument.

assertion.quantifiers: For the actual non-CM case and actual modular newform/Jacobian delivered by the previous argument.

assertion.exceptional_cases: Z may be zero-dimensional. The isogeny A to B0 uses nonzero image and absolute simplicity. No reverse bounded isogeny is inferred from the complement construction.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain the nonzero same-field Hom first, take its image, construct the ground-field complement, and only afterwards apply the separate height and bounded reverse-isogeny estimates.

assertion.statement: For the original principally polarized QM surface A/K in the six-contact construction, one finite Galois field L contains K, defines all ordered Hom groups between its conjugates, has degree at most D and is unramified outside T; the full geometric endomorphism algebra of A is B or M2(k) for an imaginary quadratic k.
assertion.objects: The original A, W0=Res_(K/Q) A and its actual integral endomorphism lattice; the same geometric conjugates and original principal polarization.
assertion.hypotheses: The original-datum construction supplies K/Q normal of degree<=F0=324!, A/K good outside S, K unramified outside T=S union supp(M_S(u)), and common polarized geometric point; the retained published Hodge/algebraicity and good-reduction Tate inputs apply.
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational u outside the six contacts and allowed S; all conjugates and all ordered pairs of them; every prime outside T.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero, dimension A=2, dim W0=2[K:Q]; arbitrary finite rank r of End(W0), not only rank4.
assertion.uniformity: One field L simultaneously defines the full Hom collection; its bound is uniform in u once F0 is fixed.
assertion.normalizations: Full geometric endomorphisms and integral Betti lattice; action on End(W0) rather than a chosen equivariant labeling of conjugates. Betti/Tate comparison is not claimed Galois equivariant.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Every residue prime is covered by choosing an auxiliary Tate prime different from it. The torsion-free mod3 kernel proof applies to arbitrary r. CM and non-CM outcomes are separated; no replacement isogenous A is substituted.
assertion.limit_order: Construct W0 and its finite Galois action first, kill that action by its mod3 kernel, then descend block Hom maps and identify full Hodge endomorphisms.

assertion.statement: For an abelian variety over a characteristic-zero field, rational matrix units give abelian image factors over that same field, mutually isogenous via off-diagonal units; complementary images sum by an isogeny.
assertion.objects: The original A/L with its L-defined M2(k) action, diagonal idempotents e11,e22 and a common positive integer denominator m.
assertion.hypotheses: The idempotents and matrix units belong to End_L^0(A); the image construction uses properness, geometric connectedness, and smoothness of finite-type group schemes in characteristic zero (the retained Cartier input).
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational matrix-unit system on this same abelian variety and every common denominator clearing it.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic zero; here dim A=2 and the two matrix-unit factors have equal positive dimension.
assertion.uniformity: All images and maps are defined over L; no further field extension is introduced.
assertion.constants: Choose any positive integer m clearing the matrix-unit denominators; no uniform isogeny-degree bound is asserted by this algebraic construction.
assertion.normalizations: X_i=image(m e_ii); addition p and tuple q satisfy pq=[m] and qp=[m]. Off-diagonal units provide rational isomorphisms between X_i, and End^0(X_i)=e_ii End^0(A)e_ii.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Images do not depend on the chosen denominator. This is not a polarization-preserving isogeny assertion and does not give a good-reduction field bound or a quantitative isogeny estimate.
assertion.limit_order: First obtain L-defined full endomorphisms; then clear denominators, construct the images, and use the matrix-unit identities. Dimension two gives elliptic factors; the corner k gives CM.

assertion.statement: Obtain the Gaussian fixed-field weighted Hecke prime estimate uniformly in rational progression moduli q<=log(X)^B.
assertion.objects: E=Q(i); fixed finite-order ray character chi of modulus m; rational Dirichlet rho modulo q; theta(a)=chi(a)rho(Na), a ray character modulo m(q), whose finite modulus norm is at most Nm*q^2.
assertion.hypotheses: For q<=(log X)^B and sqrtX<=Y<=X, Nm*q^2<=(log Y)^(2B+1) for sufficiently large X depending only on m,B. Mitsui applies with fixed K=E and A=2B+1, uniformly over rho,q. SmallY<sqrtX handled by elementary ideal von Mangoldt sum bound. Fixed bounded X absorbed. Principal indicator checked by inducing character.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: For q<=(log X)^B and sqrtX<=Y<=X, Nm*q^2<=(log Y)^(2B+1) for sufficiently large X depending only on m,B. Mitsui applies with fixed K=E and A=2B+1, uniformly over rho,q. SmallY<sqrtX handled by elementary ideal von Mangoldt sum bound. Fixed bounded X absorbed. Principal indicator checked by inducing character.
assertion.uniformity: Subtract the smoothed prime sums at x*exp(h) and x to prove unsmoothing for complex characters; bound prime powers of exponent>=2 by O_E(sqrtY log^2(2Y)); replace error atY by Xexp(-c sqrtlogX). Optional primitive-to-imprimitive restoration costs O_chi(log(q+2)log(Y+2)). Any fixed log-power saving follows. No extra Fogels external application is consumed by this proof.
assertion.constants: For a fixed number field and finite-order ray characters of logarithmically bounded modulus norm, the weighted prime-ideal sum has main term X exactly for the character induced from the trivial primitive character and error X exp(-c sqrt(log X)), uniformly in the permitted characters and moduli, with ineffective fixed-data constants.
assertion.normalizations: Normalized ideal norm; Lambda_K(p^j)=log Np for j>=1; finite-order ray characters extended by zero at excluded primes; all residue degrees included; principal means induced by the trivial primitive character. Fixed field and logarithmic exponent. Constants ineffective.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Complex characters require the explicit unsmoothing; prime powers and omitted Euler factors are removed separately.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the Gaussian ray data and B; use the conductor norm bound for sqrt(X)<=Y<=X, then treat short Y separately.

assertion.statement: Obtain the normalized majorant mean on fixed-relative-length intervals required by the boundary cutoff.
assertion.objects: Take one affine divisor-sum factor W*x+b and a fixed relative-length interval I in the enlarged ambient domain; nu0=1 is immediate if no anchor is present.
assertion.hypotheses: Freeze v and epsilon before the size limit. b is a unit modulo W, the smooth cutoff is fixed and the sieve exponent is sufficiently small. Singleton convex-body specialization has no pairwise degeneracy condition to check. Use the same cutoff normalization as in nu0; its total-mass normalization is one. At primes dividing W, normalization cancels the unit local factor.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Freeze v and epsilon before the size limit. b is a unit modulo W, the smooth cutoff is fixed and the sieve exponent is sufficiently small. Singleton convex-body specialization has no pairwise degeneracy condition to check. Use the same cutoff normalization as in nu0; its total-mass normalization is one. At primes dividing W, normalization cancels the unit local factor.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain E1_I*nu0=|I|/n plus the stated iterated errors. Together with weighted L2 this gives O(epsilon)+cutoff error+size error for boundary strips.
assertion.constants: The normalized divisor-sum convex-body estimate gives the mean of a single unit-residue affine majorant over a fixed relative-length interval, with the stated iterated cutoff and size errors. This is a singleton specialization of the source estimate.
assertion.normalizations: This is a specialization of a proved divisor-sum/convex-body estimate, not a separately named interval-prime theorem. No claim that global L1 or global Gowers smallness alone implies the interval mean.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Global L1 normalization alone is insufficient; use the one-form convex-domain divisor-sum estimate.
assertion.limit_order: Freeze v and epsilon before size; only then pass to the outer cutoff limit.

assertion.statement: Bound the first and second shifted-majorant moments in the boundary argument and obtain weighted L2 control.
assertion.objects: In a fixed enlarged ambient interval without wrap, isolate at most one constant-shift factor nu0. Set F(x)=E_m product_i nu_i(x+P_i(m)). Apply to nu0*F, nu0*F^2, nu0.
assertion.hypotheses: In F^2 use independent m and mprime; every pairwise difference of the nonconstant shifts, including across the two copies, is nonconstant. All degrees and counts are fixed, coefficients fall within A^C, and the parameter box lengths exceed the required logarithmic lower bound. The sieve exponent is chosen small enough for this enlarged moment family.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: In F^2 use independent m and mprime; every pairwise difference of the nonconstant shifts, including across the two copies, is nonconstant. All degrees and counts are fixed, coefficients fall within A^C, and the parameter box lengths exceed the required logarithmic lower bound. The sieve exponent is chosen small enough for this enlarged moment family.
assertion.uniformity: The three moments give E nu0*(F-1)^2=o(1). Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz reduces any interval-strip mass to E1_I*nu0; V6-GA-GT-INTERVAL-MEAN supplies that mean.
assertion.constants: The polynomial-forms estimate for the normalized divisor-sum majorant gives the stated asymptotic for a fixed family whose pairwise shift differences are nonconstant, over the full cyclic base variable and permitted parameter boxes, with cutoff-then-size errors.
assertion.normalizations: The source theorem averages x over the whole cyclic group; no x-subinterval conclusion is quoted. Errors retain cutoff-then-size order, o_(v to infinity)(1)+o_v(1).
assertion.exceptional_cases: The global cyclic moment estimate does not by itself imply interval mean control; the latter is separately imported.
assertion.limit_order: Freeze polynomial family, complexity and cutoff before size; apply the second-moment estimate to independent copies.

assertion.constants: The polynomial generalized von Neumann estimate makes the stated multilinear average small when one factor has the required small local box norm and all factors meet the ordinary-majorant domination and polynomial nondegeneracy hypotheses.

assertion.statement: Pass to the conjugated rational subgroup quotient on each periodic class and recenter the translated test function there.
assertion.objects: H_j=gamma_j^(-1)*G-prime*gamma_j; Lambda_j=H_j intersect Gamma; h_j=gamma_j^(-1)*g-prime*gamma_j. F_jk(x Lambda_j)=F(a_jk*gamma_j*x Gamma).
assertion.hypotheses: Reduced gamma_j has rational coordinates of height M^O(1); a_jk=epsilon(n_jk) has bounded M-power coordinates. The output subgroup basis and lattice satisfy the published claim.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Reduced gamma_j has rational coordinates of height M^O(1); a_jk=epsilon(n_jk) has bounded M-power coordinates. The output subgroup basis and lattice satisfy the published claim.
assertion.uniformity: Obtain basis rationality M^C2, total M^(-aB+C2)-equidistribution and Lip norm M^C2. Account for commensurable lattices and finite-index losses; conjugation is not an isometry of the original quotients. Subtract each new quotient Haar mean, including the dimension-zero case. The claim is used for a general weight through separate mean/minor-arc hypotheses, not by extending the Möbius theorem.
assertion.constants: The published quantitative conjugation claim transfers a rational subgroup orbit to the conjugated quotient with the actual intersection lattice, controlling rationality, equidistribution and Lipschitz losses by fixed powers of the height bound.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The quotient comparison is not an isometry; finite-index and Lipschitz losses and the zero-dimensional case remain explicit.
assertion.limit_order: Fix B and the resulting M, then permit fixed powers of M in the new basis, metric and equidistribution losses.

assertion.statement: Apply polynomial recurrence to the dense set of type-I phases d! beta_j r^j while preserving the short-arc factor.
assertion.objects: Polynomial r -> d!*beta_j*r^j modulo one on [ceil(R)] for each 1<=j<=d.
assertion.hypotheses: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.
assertion.quantifiers: For every choice of the application parameters satisfying these hypotheses at the named current consumer; no conclusion is claimed for a different proof stage.
assertion.parameter_range: Selected r have eta-power density. Values lie in an arc of length <=2*eta^(-C5)*(R/N)^j. R<=2*N^(2/3), sufficiently large K_rec, and the large-R branch ensure arc length at most half density. Small R is treated internally by multiplying by r^d.
assertion.uniformity: Retain the arc-length factor in the published smoothness conclusion; the leading coefficient then has N^(-j), not merely R^(-j), accuracy. Additional factorial and product of nonzero bounded integers yield one character.
assertion.constants: If a polynomial phase takes values in a sufficiently short arc on a positive-density subset of an interval, the recurrence lemma gives a bounded nonzero integer multiple with a C-infinity bound retaining the arc-length factor and a power loss in the density.
assertion.normalizations: G connected, simply connected and nilpotent; Gamma discrete cocompact; filtration by closed connected rational subgroups; adapted rational Malcev basis; C-infinity norm in the binomial basis modulo one; Lipschitz norm includes supremum norm. Nontrivial horizontal characters are integer-lattice characters annihilating commutators and Gamma.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The arc factor is needed to recover N^-j precision and cannot be discarded.
assertion.limit_order: Check that the arc is at most half the density in the large-R range; treat small R before applying recurrence.

assertion.statement: The actual sections J^2 q_i, already regular at every codimension-one point, extend uniquely across codimension two on the maximal stack.
assertion.objects: The regular Noetherian maximal D210 Deligne-Mumford stack and its invertible square-dualizing line with rational sections J^2 q0,J^2 q1.
assertion.hypotheses: The stack is regular and flat over the base. The line is invertible, the sections are regular on the generic fibre, and the separately proved vertical valuation bounds give regularity at vertical codimension-one points.
assertion.quantifiers: Both displayed sections, on every regular etale chart and every codimension-one point.
assertion.parameter_range: The actual maximal stack, including primes dividing210; no tame coarse quotient is assumed there.
assertion.uniformity: The same rational sections and line extend; no rescaling beyond the already fixed J^2.
assertion.constants: J remains2765952000; no new height constant.
assertion.normalizations: Trivialize the line on affine regular etale charts; apply the source with M=R, a free rank-one and hence reflexive module.
assertion.exceptional_cases: This does not construct a coarse-model line bundle, supply the valuation bounds, or extend a general nonreflexive sheaf.
assertion.limit_order: Choose an etale scheme atlas of the regular Noetherian Deligne-Mumford maximal stack and trivialize the invertible square-dualizing line on affine open charts. Each connected regular chart is a normal domain. The generic bicanonical section is regular at horizontal height-one primes; the separate vertical valuation calculation proves it at vertical height-one primes. Apply Tag0AVB with the free rank-one module, which is reflexive, to obtain a unique regular section on each chart. The extensions agree on etale overlaps because they agree on the dense generic fibre and the line is locally free on a reduced flat atlas. Descent for sections gives the unique section on the stack. No coarse-model pullback or tame argument at bad primes is used.

assertion.statement: There are s>=1 and one D in Z[e,n,z1,...,zs] such that for all ordinary e,n in N including0, machine e halts on n exactly when D(e,n,z)=0 has an integer witness tuple.
assertion.objects: A fixed effective syntactic enumeration of machines, ordinary parameter pair(e,n), and integer witness tuple z.
assertion.hypotheses: The universal halting relation is computably enumerable; positive witness conversion uses the four-square theorem explicitly recorded on sourcep2.
assertion.quantifiers: One fixed s and D, then every e,n>=0; existential witnesses range independently over Z.
assertion.parameter_range: Nonnegative ordinary machine/input indices, not elliptic-curve coordinates; witnesses arbitrary integers.
assertion.uniformity: D and its arity do not depend on e or n; no extraction of a separate polynomial for each machine.
assertion.constants: Finite s>=1, with no claimed explicit size or degree bound.
assertion.normalizations: Apply source to(a,b)↦machine a-1 halts on b-1 for a,b>0; substitute a=e+1,b=n+1 and each positive witness y=1+z1^2+z2^2+z3^2+z4^2.
assertion.exceptional_cases: e=0 and n=0 are included by the shifts. If no positive witnesses occur, add an unused integer witness to ensure s>=1.
assertion.limit_order: Fix machine enumeration and enumerable binary predicate; fix R; make polynomial substitutions; only then vary e,n.

original_use.reason: The universal positive binary halting predicate is enumerable by direct simulation. Apply the Basic Theorem once, then substitute ordinary index shifts and positive witnesses as1+four squares. Surjectivity of this substitution onto all positive integers gives both directions. This is a fixed representation theorem, not merely the unsolvability corollary.
